questions.article: A researcher selected 23 guinea pigs from one habitat and 19 wild cavies from another habitat at random in Venezuela. A held of a specifc size within each habitat was divided into equally-sized virtual squares, and the animals were allowed to wander in the field for a fixed amount of time. To observe their behavior, the researcher counted the number of times the guinea pigs and wild cavies crossed the virtual squares in their held during early adolescence and again during late adolescence. The researcher found that in early adolescence, the number of virtual squares the wild cavies crossed was significantly more than the number of virtual squares the quinea pigs crossed, The researcher also found that the number of virtual squares crossed by both the wild cavies and the guinea pigs decreased from early adolescence to late adolescence. Based on the researcher's findings, which of the following statements is an appropriate conclusion that can be drawn from this study?

options.name: A
options.content: the statistically significant difference in behavior between the two age groups was caused by the differences in habitat.

options.name: B
options.content: The statistically significant difference in behavior between the two age groups was caused by aging.

options.name: C
options.content: The statistically significant difference in behavior during early adolescence between the two groups of animals can be generalized to all guinea pigs and wild cavies.

options.name: D
options.content: Tho statistically significant difference in behavior during early adolescence between the two groups of animals can only be generalized to the habitats in the study.

questions.correct: Tho statistically significant difference in behavior during early adolescence between the two groups of animals can only be generalized to the habitats in the study.
